subject: ventures/bonus-depreciation-calculator
professional: a CPA who prepares business returns and fixed-asset schedules (Form 4562); first checks: the OBBBA 2025 and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 2026 Section 179 limit and phase-out, the 100% bonus acquisition-date cutoff (after Jan 19, 2025), the Pub 946 Table A-1 first-year MACRS rates, what property qualifies for Section 179 versus bonus, and whether the Section 179 path also depreciates the basis left over the limit

evidence.correctness: Independent script (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/2d2e6a91-ab4e-5afb-9d66-7868d2f21338/scratchpad/bdc/run.mjs, `node run.mjs`) recomputed outputs from the methods, not from the author's tables. MACRS first-year rates derived as DB-rate/life x 0.5 (200% DB for 3/5/7/10-year, 150% DB for 15/20-year, IRC 168(b)) give 33,333.33/20,000/14,285.71/10,000/5,000/3,750 per 100,000; the tool gives 33,330/20,000/14,290/10,000/5,000/3,750, i.e. Pub 946 Table A-1's rounded 33.33%/14.29%, so pass. Section 179 constants 2,500,000/4,000,000 (OBBBA, tax years beginning after 2024) and 2,560,000/4,090,000 (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 for 2026), own knowledge, irs.gov not fetched: match. 2026 phase-out by hand: 4,500,000 total purchases -> limit 2,560,000-410,000 = 2,150,000 (tool 2,150,000); full phase-out at 6,650,000 (tool 0 at 6,650,000, 1 at 6,649,999). Income-limited case (250k 7-year at 80%, 120k income, 24%): basis 200,000, bonus usable 120,000 / NOL 80,000 / saving 28,800, 179 carryforward 80,000, MACRS 28,580 / saving 6,859.20: all match. Not a 3: (a) the Section 179 path elects up to the limit and drops the rest of the basis, which a preparer would bonus or depreciate in the same year (IRC 168(k)(1)(A) applies to the basis after 179, Pub 946 ch. 3): a 3,000,000 asset in 2025 shows 179 saving 525,000 where 179+bonus gives 630,000 and 179+MACRS 546,000; (b) the 15-year option is labelled 'land improvements' yet the 179 path fully expenses 200,000 of it with no warning, while Pub 946 ch. 2 lists land improvements (paved parking areas, fences, docks) as not Section 179 property; (c) 40% business use of non-listed equipment is told bonus is unavailable, though the 50% test bars bonus only for listed property (IRC 280F(b)(1), 168(k)(2)(D)(i)).
evidence.completeness: Claimed features run end to end: three-path comparison, eligible basis x business use, 2025/2026 Section 179 limit and phase-out against other purchases, income cap with 179 carryforward vs NOL flag, MACRS year-1 and remaining basis, >50% business-use flag, worked example, opt-out local usage counts, comparison page, sitemap/robots/llms.txt. `node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs bonus-depreciation-calculator`: no placeholder or retired origin in what ships. No stubs or TODOs. The README's 'What this does not cover' list matches what is missing (ADS, luxury-auto caps, carryforward valuation).
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/bonus-depreciation-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 45 tests, 45 pass, 150 ms. Six seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 15-year rate 0.05->0.075 SURVIVED, 7-year rate 0.1429->0.125 SURVIVED (the test compares the output with FIRST_YEAR_MACRS_RATE itself, so any table value passes), bonus cash saving deduction*rate instead of usable*rate SURVIVED (the cash-saving test uses income above the deduction); 2026 constants, the <=50% boundary and the 179 income cap CAUGHT. 3 of 6 survive: the 179 arithmetic is pinned by hand-worked numbers, the MACRS table and bonus income cap on cash savings are not.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (268 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, index.html script. Pure functions, no dependencies, constants in two named tables, the NOL vs 179-carryforward split kept in separate functions on purpose and documented. Defects: an unknown tax year silently falls back to 2025 rules (calc.mjs:134, pinned by a test) rather than refusing; blank taxable income becomes 0 (index.html:244), so a user who skips the field sees every path flagged NOL with zero saving and no prompt; at <=50% business use the stats line still prints bonus and 179 cash savings (index.html:249) under the finding that says they do not apply; comment typo '$2.5,000,000' (calc.mjs:33) and the comment calls all six classes 200% DB (calc.mjs:49) though 15/20-year are 150% DB.
evidence.claims: Backed: OBBBA 100% bonus after Jan 19, 2025 and its permanence; 2025/2026 Section 179 figures; NOL 80% limit and no carryback (IRC 172 post-TCJA); 179 income limit and indefinite carryforward (IRC 179(b)(3)); per-class bonus election-out; MACRS Table A-1 rates; disclaimer in README, page footer, FAQ and llms.txt; privacy line matches usage.mjs (local storage, DNT/GPC, opt-out button). Not backed: 'Property used 50% or less for business does not qualify for bonus depreciation or Section 179 at all' (README.md:49, index.html:96, FAQ, calc.mjs:44 and the finding text) is true for Section 179 and for listed property, not for bonus on non-listed property; the 15-year option labelled 'land improvements' (index.html:91) in a tool that offers a Section 179 election on it; '200%-declining-balance' for all classes (calc.mjs:49).
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: an owner or preparer weighing a single equipment purchase gets a correct side-by-side of the current-year deduction and cash saving, the phase-out and the NOL vs 179-carryforward distinction, enough for a first conversation. Hit in the first hour by a CPA: no acquisition date, so a 2025 asset acquired under a binding contract before Jan 20, 2025 is shown at 100% bonus instead of 40% (OBBBA transition); the 179 path ignores the basis over the limit (179 + bonus on the remainder is the usual combination); no mid-quarter convention warning; a single flat rate stands for the whole tax effect; no 179 eligibility check for real property and land improvements.
evidence.domain: Method matches practice for: the phase-out against total section 179 property placed in service, the income limit producing a 179 carryforward not an NOL, bonus not income-limited, half-year Table A-1 rates, basis times business use. Departures: the >50% test is applied to bonus for all property instead of listed property only; land improvements are offered with a full 179 election; the 179 path does not combine with bonus or MACRS on the remaining basis; the 2025 acquisition-date cutoff (40% vs 100%) is described in the FAQ but never asked for or applied.

defects.what: The Section 179 path elects up to the dollar limit and drops the rest of the basis; a preparer takes bonus (or MACRS) on the remainder in the same year (IRC 168(k)(1)(A), Pub 946 ch. 3). A 3,000,000 asset in 2025 at 21% shows a 179 saving of 525,000 where 179 + bonus gives 630,000 (179 + MACRS 546,000), so the comparison understates the 179 path whenever basis exceeds the limit after phase-out.

The 15-year option is labelled 'land improvements' and the Section 179 path fully expenses it with no warning; Pub 946 ch. 2 lists land improvements (paved parking areas, fences, docks, bridges) as not section 179 property.

The >50% business-use test is applied to bonus depreciation for all property; it forces ADS (and bars bonus) only for listed property (IRC 280F(b)(1), 168(k)(2)(D)(i)). Section 179's >50% requirement is stated correctly. The same overstatement is in README.md:49, index.html:96, the FAQ and the finding text.

No acquisition date: for tax year 2025 every asset gets 100% bonus, though property acquired (binding contract) before Jan 20, 2025 and placed in service in 2025 gets 40%. The FAQ explains the cutoff, but the result does not ask or state the assumption.

Three of six seeded mutants survive: the MACRS rate test compares output with FIRST_YEAR_MACRS_RATE itself (any table value passes; 7-year and 15-year changes survived), and the bonus cash-saving test uses income above the deduction, so computing saving on the full deduction instead of the usable part survives.
At 50% or less business use the stats line and the three cards still print bonus and Section 179 cash savings under a finding saying they do not apply.

Blank taxable income silently becomes 0, so a user who skips the field sees every path flagged as NOL / carryforward with a zero saving and no prompt; an unknown tax year silently uses the 2025 rules.

Comment errors: '$2.5,000,000' for 2,500,000 (line 33) and all six classes called 200% declining balance (line 49) though 15- and 20-year property use 150% DB (IRC 168(b)(2)(A)); the rate values themselves are right.

No mid-quarter convention warning: if more than 40% of the year's depreciable basis is placed in service in Q4, Table A-1 half-year rates do not apply to the plain-MACRS column (IRC 168(d)(3), Pub 946 Tables A-2 to A-5).

verdict: The arithmetic it does is right: MACRS first-year rates derived from the method match Pub 946 Table A-1, the 2025 and 2026 Section 179 limits and phase-out (including the exact zero point at 6,650,000 for 2026) and the income cap with its 179 carryforward vs NOL split all recompute to the dollar, and the disclaimer and privacy claims are backed. It falls below the bar on domain rules a CPA would hit at once: the Section 179 path throws away the basis over the limit instead of bonusing or depreciating it (a 3,000,000 asset is understated by 105,000 of saving), the 15-year 'land improvements' class gets a full Section 179 election that Pub 946 does not allow, the 50% business-use bar is applied to bonus for all property rather than listed property, and 2025 assets are always given 100% bonus with no acquisition date. Tests pin the 179 math but not the MACRS table or the bonus income cap on cash savings: three of six seeded mutants survive.
